compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional project, a four-person team has ten weeks to rebuild an internal system with sparse documentation and a rough brief. Either person might work independently. The role, prior experience, deadline and available information help explain how the work proceeds.

Introversion describes a preference for directing attention and energy inward. Thinking describes a preference for weighing decisions against consistent criteria. Neither tells you who will be quieter, calmer or more independent.

The difference runs on two axes. S/N compares material: connections and possibility, or observable fact and prior experience. J/P compares the outward stance: forming an arrangement and a conclusion, or keeping options and adjusting when new information arrives. The same person may draw on the other kind of information in a different task; what matters is which side gets relied on more.

Two colleagues can draw on the same records or reach similar conclusions, even if they place different weight on a pattern or a specific observation. Both can check documents, take measurements and see whether a result can be reproduced.

### INTJ and ISTP: the same deliverable, two checking angles

Put the same rebuild plan and the same batch of operating records on the table. One angle watches the goal and the criteria that can be checked in common: does this plan meet what was agreed in advance? Could a colleague take it over and run it? Where are the gaps, and what would closing them cost? The basis for judgement is mostly the commonly confirmed definitions, acceptance conditions and delivery requirements.

The other angle watches the reasoning and its conditions: does this approach contain steps that do nothing? Would it still hold with a different data set, in a different environment? Which premises does the conclusion depend on? The basis is mostly whether the structure is coherent, whether the conditions are stated, and whether it can be reproduced step by step.

Both angles can find problems. Checked against acceptance requirements, a plan may turn out ingenious but short of the delivery conditions; checked for structure and premises, a plan may meet the standard while resting on fragile assumptions. The two checks can run together, and who does which depends on role and expertise.

Keep the counterexamples. In a field someone has worked for years, either may align with industry norms unprompted, because rework is expensive; in front of familiar equipment or code, either may judge directly from experience, because the deadline leaves no room for item-by-item verification. These differences come from training, duty and deadline, not from four letters.

S/N describes a preference in how information is taken in. In type dynamics, J/P indicates whether the outward-facing process is a judging or perceiving process. For INTJ it is auxiliary Te, a judging process. For ISTP it is auxiliary Se, a perceiving process.

Both stacks carry Ni and Se, in different seats: Ni dominant and Se inferior in INTJ; Se auxiliary and Ni third in ISTP. The relative order is reversed — it is not one slot exchanged. The judging pair changes wholesale: Te auxiliary and Fi third in INTJ; Ti dominant and Fe inferior in ISTP.

Sharing a name is not sharing a view. But it does not follow that the two naturally agree on the facts — disagreement can sit in the material itself, and aligning information first remains necessary.

compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The following fictional scenes illustrate different questions people can ask with the same information. Promotion decisions should use the role requirements and documented work. A potential partnership depends on its terms and the people involved. Personality type does not substitute for either assessment.

If both sit on the review panel, having each write a conclusion and its reasons independently before comparing notes preserves more information than discussing sentence by sentence; whoever speaks first tends to set the wording for the whole discussion.

### INTJ and ISTP: one promotion slot, two candidates

(Fictional scene) The same material for both: two candidates compete for one slot. Candidate A led two cross-department projects to completion independently; one ran six weeks late, during which the external interface partner changed systems; in that period A located and solved an interface problem that others had circled for three months, and the project brief, issue ticket, review notes and release records are all traceable. Candidate B delivered steadily with no delays, though the scope of every project was set by someone else; B led one cross-department coordination with meeting notes, but left no document defining a problem independently.

The first panel member lays out what this level requires: defining a problem independently, coordinating more than three departments, carrying the result. Then matches the record item by item: A has a project brief for the first, coordination records for the second, release and retrospective records for the third; B lacks a record of independently defining a problem for the first, and the number of departments for the second and the result accountability for the third still need checking. The three items have to be written separately: which is proven, which is merely under-evidenced, which genuinely falls short. The delay itself does not prove a coordination failure; what matters is what A did during it.

The second panel member looks at the weight of the specific problem: what constrained that interface issue, which approaches were tried, why this one finally held, whether someone else would also have been stuck. That judgement likewise has to rest on reviewable evidence — the reproduction steps in the issue ticket, the trade-off reasons in the review notes, the operating data after release — not on impression.

The two conclusions may agree while resting on different grounds, and both grounds can go into the review record. The risks are symmetrical: scoring only against a checklist may select someone with complete paperwork and no hard problem-solving; going only by the impression of one difficult problem may select someone who resembles the reviewer. Gaps both identify get verified first; whether they affect the decision still follows the post standard.

A workable check is to align both candidates' evidence on one sheet before the review: the same measure, the same time window, the same source of evidence, with gaps left blank rather than filled from impression. Discussing the blanks first is usually more productive than arguing the conclusion first.

### INTJ and ISTP: an old classmate proposes starting a studio

(Fictional scene) A classmate not seen for ten years arrives with a business plan and proposes going into business together. One asks what the studio should look like in three years, how equity is split, under what conditions someone exits, and who decides when opinions diverge; the other asks where the first order comes from, which equipment has to be added, who owns which step, and what happens in the busy season when hands are short.

Either set of questions can be heard by the other as a flaw: one sounds like overthinking, the other like short horizons. In fact both are shrinking the uncontrollable part, one working back from the end state, the other forward from current resources. The blind spots mirror each other too: talking only about the end state can underestimate start-up cash flow; talking only about the present can miss exit and disagreement mechanisms.

A dry run can come first: take a mock order or an internal sample and run quotation, scheduling, delivery and rework all the way through, agreeing in advance the division of work, the cost ceiling and the stopping conditions. Before taking a real order, confirm compliance requirements, the contracting and receiving entity, and each side's liability, then decide whether to trial. A dry run creates no external commitment, and it does not mean there is no risk.

compare_blocks.body:
The first misread comes from independence. Both may work without someone watching, but the content differs: one may not need anyone to set the direction, the other may not need anyone to show them how. Judging by "he will not take advice" misreads both; independence may also be a job requirement rather than evidence of personality.

The second takes actions as the test. Writing documents does not mean a preference for J, and working with your hands does not mean a preference for P — both are mostly the product of training and duty, and neither indicates S/N, J/P or any other dimension on its own. A preference is also not an ability, and cannot by itself decide whether someone can do a task.

The third treats talking about standards as bureaucracy and talking about feel as unprofessional. That ranking is especially harmful in reviews and hiring: it rewards one style of expression and blinds the panel to the judgement the other person has already made. Sharing Ni and Se does not mean the two see the same facts either; disagreement may sit in the material itself.

The difference runs on two axes. S/N compares material: connections and possibility, or observable fact and prior experience. J/P compares the outward stance: forming an arrangement and a conclusion, or keeping options and adjusting when new information arrives. The same person may draw on the other kind of information in a different task; what matters is which side gets relied on more.

Two colleagues can draw on the same records or reach similar conclusions, even if they place different weight on a pattern or a specific observation. Both can check documents, take measurements and see whether a result can be reproduced.

Put the same rebuild plan and the same batch of operating records on the table. One angle watches the goal and the criteria that can be checked in common: does this plan meet what was agreed in advance? Could a colleague take it over and run it? Where are the gaps, and what would closing them cost? The basis for judgement is mostly the commonly confirmed definitions, acceptance conditions and delivery requirements.

The other angle watches the reasoning and its conditions: does this approach contain steps that do nothing? Would it still hold with a different data set, in a different environment? Which premises does the conclusion depend on? The basis is mostly whether the structure is coherent, whether the conditions are stated, and whether it can be reproduced step by step.

Both angles can find problems. Checked against acceptance requirements, a plan may turn out ingenious but short of the delivery conditions; checked for structure and premises, a plan may meet the standard while resting on fragile assumptions. (Fictional scene) The same material for both: two candidates compete for one slot. Candidate A led two cross-department projects to completion independently; one ran six weeks late, during which the external interface partner changed systems; in that period A located and solved an interface problem that others had circled for three months, and the project brief, issue ticket, review notes and release records are all traceable. Candidate B delivered steadily with no delays, though the scope of every project was set by someone else; B led one cross-department coordination with meeting notes, but left no document defining a problem independently.

The first panel member lays out what this level requires: defining a problem independently, coordinating more than three departments, carrying the result. Then matches the record item by item: A has a project brief for the first, coordination records for the second, release and retrospective records for the third; B lacks a record of independently defining a problem for the first, and the number of departments for the second and the result accountability for the third still need checking. The delay itself does not prove a coordination failure; what matters is what A did during it.

The second panel member looks at the weight of the specific problem: what constrained that interface issue, which approaches were tried, why this one finally held, whether someone else would also have been stuck. A workable check is to align both candidates' evidence on one sheet before the review: the same measure, the same time window, the same source of evidence, with gaps left blank rather than filled from impression. (Fictional scene) A classmate not seen for ten years arrives with a business plan and proposes going into business together. A dry run can come first: take a mock order or an internal sample and run quotation, scheduling, delivery and rework all the way through, agreeing in advance the division of work, the cost ceiling and the stopping conditions. Gaps both identify get verified first; whether they affect the decision still follows the post standard.

A workable check is to align both candidates' evidence on one sheet before the review: the same measure, the same time window, the same source of evidence, with gaps left blank rather than filled from impression. Discussing the blanks first is usually more productive than arguing the conclusion first.

### INTJ and ISTP: an old classmate proposes starting a studio

(Fictional scene) A classmate not seen for ten years arrives with a business plan and proposes going into business together. One asks what the studio should look like in three years, how equity is split, under what conditions someone exits, and who decides when opinions diverge; the other asks where the first order comes from, which equipment has to be added, who owns which step, and what happens in the busy season when hands are short.

Either set of questions can be heard by the other as a flaw: one sounds like overthinking, the other like short horizons. In fact both are shrinking the uncontrollable part, one working back from the end state, the other forward from current resources. The blind spots mirror each other too: talking only about the end state can underestimate start-up cash flow; talking only about the present can miss exit and disagreement mechanisms.

A dry run can come first: take a mock order or an internal sample and run quotation, scheduling, delivery and rework all the way through, agreeing in advance the division of work, the cost ceiling and the stopping conditions. Before taking a real order, confirm compliance requirements, the contracting and receiving entity, and each side's liability, then decide whether to trial. A dry run creates no external commitment, and it does not mean there is no risk.

sections.body_md:
The first misread comes from independence. Both may work without someone watching, but the content differs: one may not need anyone to set the direction, the other may not need anyone to show them how. Judging by "he will not take advice" misreads both; independence may also be a job requirement rather than evidence of personality.

The second takes actions as the test. Writing documents does not mean a preference for J, and working with your hands does not mean a preference for P — both are mostly the product of training and duty, and neither indicates S/N, J/P or any other dimension on its own. A preference is also not an ability, and cannot by itself decide whether someone can do a task.

The third treats talking about standards as bureaucracy and talking about feel as unprofessional. That ranking is especially harmful in reviews and hiring: it rewards one style of expression and blinds the panel to the judgement the other person has already made. Sharing Ni and Se does not mean the two see the same facts either; disagreement may sit in the material itself.

items.answer:
Both types share Thinking. In a fictional project review, one useful question is whether a proposal meets the agreed criteria. Another is whether the reasoning still holds if a condition changes. Those checks can illustrate Te and Ti in the model, and either reviewer can use both.

In a real disagreement, one may say this does not meet the level we defined, the other that this conclusion fails under a different condition. Who is right depends on evidence and conditions, not on whose phrasing sounds more professional; both types can use measurement, reproduction and document checks.
items.question: Is the split about watching acceptance criteria or about the conditions under which reasoning holds?

items.answer:
The judging pair: Te auxiliary and Fi third in INTJ, against Ti dominant and Fe inferior in ISTP.

In the four-function notation used here, INTJ is Ni–Te–Fi–Se and ISTP is Ti–Se–Ni–Fe. Ni and Se appear on both sides, but as dominant and inferior in INTJ and auxiliary and third in ISTP — the relative order reversed, not one slot exchanged; the attitude of the third process has other labelling versions.
items.question: They share Ni and Se — which judging pair is replaced?

items.answer:
They do, and they show that ability can be trained, that a preference does not disappear because of it, and that doing or not doing something cannot assign a type.

An ISTP writing documents may be setting out the structure clearly; an INTJ taking equipment apart may be testing an existing hypothesis. But motive cannot be inferred backwards from the action. What discriminates better is what you base "this is good enough to stop" on across comparable situations, and how far duty and deadline allowed you to go.
items.question: An ISTP writes long documents, an INTJ takes equipment apart by hand — do the counterexamples hold?

items.answer:
Not the same kind of evidence: one matched the record against the requirements of the level, the other looked at the difficulty and quality of a specific problem.

The first has to be able to say which item has a record and which is missing; the second must also cite reviewable evidence such as the issue ticket, review notes and reproduction steps. Gaps both identify get verified first, and whether they affect the decision still follows the post standard; type enters no scoring sheet.
items.question: In a promotion review, what did each panel member look at?

items.answer:
Any team can disagree about what counts as finished. One person may point to the agreed acceptance criteria, while another asks whether the underlying problem was solved. Either type can raise either concern.

A workable approach writes "done" as two lines — one externally acceptable condition, one internal structural condition — and agrees who judges and against which record. Both types can accept the other's phrasing, depending on role and task requirements.
